description: Enhanced OpenAI’s global web experience by expanding localization support and implementing comprehensive right-to-left (RTL) capabilities. Built a new language selector with locale and language search, developed supporting Tailwind utilities, and updated core components and interaction patterns to ensure a consistent experience across Arabic, Urdu, Farsi, and other localized interfaces.

sections.title: RTL Support
sections.text: Led RTL (right-to-left) support across the platform by identifying and resolving UI inconsistencies, refactoring core CSS architecture, and migrating from physical to logical styling primitives. Audited and refactored numerous core React components to address RTL-specific issues in interactive behaviors, including keyboard navigation, sliders, and dynamic dropdowns. Established RTL integration patterns with accompanying documentation to guide consistent implementation across engineering teams.

Engineered a Tailwind-based abstraction layer to eliminate manual left/right styling across the codebase. Introduced direction-aware utilities that standardize spacing, borders, and positioning using logical CSS properties, allowing components to automatically adapt between LTR and RTL layouts without duplication or conditional styling.

sections.title: Localization
sections.text: Designed and developed a fully responsive language selector that enables users to search by both language name and locale code, making it easy to discover and switch between supported languages. Built for desktop and mobile, the experience preserves the user's active session when changing languages and was designed to scale as additional locales are introduced.
Desktop interaction states for the Language Selector.
The different states for the new Language Selector on mobile.

description: For the 2024 Google I/O Gemini Developer API Competition, Hello Monday created three interactive AI games to surround the grand prize—a retrofitted electric DeLorean. Designed to inspire developers and showcase the API's capabilities beyond the standard chatbot, I was the developer behind one of these three flagship experiences: Trivia Twister.

sections.text: Built using Gemini 1.5 Pro, the Trivia Twister app creates a dynamic six-step game by blending user topics. After an initial safety check, Gemini generates six custom trivia questions, each featuring four multiple-choice answers.

Gemini Demo Night


An exclusive brand activation in Japan gave developers hands-on access to the Gemini API's capabilities. Placed alongside other experimental AI tools, Trivia Twister served as a live, tactile case study in how advanced prompting can be instantly translated into engaging, real-time user experiences.

description: A data-driven annual report that translates complex financial performance into clear, compelling visual narratives. Custom infographics, editorial photography direction, and a print-ready layout system were developed in tandem with the digital web version.

Built around ROAM's stunning portfolio of interior and exterior spaces, the website uses a horizontal scrolling experience to create a sense of exploration and discovery. Large-scale imagery, subtle motion, and a minimal interface allow the work to take center stage while guiding users through the studio's story and projects.

OpenAI partnered with Dept to create an interactive homepage takeover that introduced generative AI through a playful, Mad Libs-inspired experience. Designed mobile-first, the project combined UX, UI, front-end development, and OpenAI API integration, all delivered within an ambitious two to three week timeline before being implemented by OpenAI's engineering team.

sections.title: The takeover
sections.text: The experience was designed to help first-time users engage with ChatGPT, especially those who weren't sure what to ask. Visitors first selected from a range of categories, after which they were presented with curated prompts that could be personalized by changing key words or phrases. The completed prompt was then sent to the ChatGPT API, returning a generated response and providing an approachable introduction to prompting and conversational AI.

sections.title: My Contribution
sections.text: I developed the final stage of the experience, where users could continue exploring ChatGPT's response by transforming it into a painting, a theatre script, or a audible bedtime story. The goal was to encourage further creativity and demonstrate how a single prompt could evolve into multiple forms of expression.

Virgin Hyperloop is developing a next-generation transportation system capable of moving passengers and cargo at airline speeds. I helped build an interactive platform that explains the technology, showcases global initiatives, and makes a complex concept easier to understand.

sections.text: A series of interactive Three.js experiences guide users through the core components of the Hyperloop system, helping explain how the technology works through exploration rather than lengthy technical content.
An interactive map highlights Hyperloop projects and partnerships around the world, providing users with a clear overview of the company's growing international presence.

An interactive route estimator compares travel times across traditional modes of transportation and Hyperloop, helping users understand the potential impact of high-speed transit on real-world journeys.
Dedicated regional pages showcase local Hyperloop initiatives, project progress, and relevant news updates, providing a closer look at development efforts around the world.

description:
During my time at Cartelle, I helped build and maintain the e-commerce platform for Scotch & Soda, developing product listing pages, product detail pages, editorial content, and campaign experiences. The platform combined commerce with a strong visual identity, using vivid imagery and custom layouts to create a more engaging shopping experience.
Following my time at Cartelle, I continued working with Scotch & Soda on the evolution of their digital platform.

sections.title: E-Commerce Platform
sections.text: I helped build and evolve the front end of the Scotch & Soda e-commerce platform, working across nearly every touchpoint of the shopping experience. From homepage campaigns and editorial content to product discovery, filtering, PDPs, checkout, and payment, I focused on creating reusable, scalable components that supported both marketing initiatives and the day-to-day needs of the commerce platform.

sections.title: Portraits
sections.text: For the Autumn campaign, we combined expansive full-bleed photography with an editorial-inspired calendar experience that highlighted the seasonal collection. Rather than relying on traditional models, the campaign featured Scotch & Soda employees and friends of the brand, pairing each look with a short personal interview to create a more authentic and human story around the collection.

sections.title: Misguiding Guide
sections.text: The Misguiding Guide was an interactive iPad experience created in collaboration with an illustrator, featuring a hand-drawn map of Amsterdam curated by a selection of local personalities. Users could freely explore the map, discover hotspots, and uncover interviews, photography, and seasonal looks, blending storytelling, fashion, and exploration into a playful digital guide.

sections.title: All Together Now
sections.text: Created for the holiday season, this campaign featured employees from across Scotch & Soda alongside members of their families, modeling pieces from the winter collection just before the company's annual Christmas celebration. Each scene could be explored in a panning view, with interactive hotspots allowing visitors to discover and shop the featured garments.

sections.title: Rewind the Night
sections.text: Designed to showcase Scotch & Soda's evening collection, this campaign used cinematic photography, video, and a timeline-driven experience to follow the progression of a night out. Visitors could jump between different moments in the evening, creating a narrative that reflected both the atmosphere and the versatility of the collection.

sections.title: Sir Safari Pop
sections.text: Created to highlight the Sir Safari Pop collection, this campaign paired bold photography with atmospheric video introductions for every chapter. Each section embraced its own visual identity while guiding visitors through the collection as it evolved from one season to the next.

description: Created for Google's Black History Month 2020 campaign, Most Searched explored influential Black figures, events, and achievements through the lens of Google Search trends. The experience combined historical context, media, and data-driven insights to celebrate individuals and moments that shaped American culture.

It was rewarding to see the campaign featured on a massive billboard just a block from my apartment. Seeing something I had worked on come to life in the real world was a memorable and unexpected moment.

description: Developed in collaboration with Nessim Higson, this project explores how typography can emerge from texture instead of traditional letterforms. Using a curated collection of glass fracture assets alongside generative crack patterns, every word becomes a unique composition that mimics the appearance of a shattered display. The result is a visual illusion that balances abstraction with legibility, encouraging users to create their own cracked-screen artwork from any word they choose.

sections.title: Setup
sections.text: The first challenge was making each composition feel unique. Fortunately, Ness had created between three and six variations for every letter, allowing each character to be selected at random. From there, I generated columns with varying widths, randomized each letter's vertical position within the canvas, and introduced subtle rotation. These small variations ensured that every word felt naturally fractured rather than mechanically assembled.

Anchor points


While the randomized letterforms worked well on their own, we felt the illusion wasn't complete—the cracks needed to continue seamlessly across the entire composition. To achieve this, Ness created an additional library of glass fracture assets, including nine vertical connectors, sixteen horizontal connectors, and dedicated corner cracks.

To align these assets, I embedded small red and blue marker pixels into every letter image. At runtime, the canvas scans each letter to locate those markers, using their coordinates as anchor points for the connecting fracture lines. Once their positions have been recorded, the marker pixels are made transparent, leaving only the finished composition visible. This approach allows the crack patterns to flow naturally between letters, making the final image feel like a single shattered screen rather than a collection of separate characters.
